    2027 NFL Draft order: Titans hold No. 1 spot as Chargers, Dolphins also fall to 1-9 in Week 11

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (386 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, the Tennessee Titans may have allowed 51 points on Sunday afternoon, but they are still in control of the No.
    • It has been revealed that the Titans fell to 1-9 on the season on Sunday afternoon in a rough 51-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium.
    • The Titans overtook the Los Angeles Chargers last week for the top spot after the Chargers finally picked up their first win of the season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the Tennessee Titans may have allowed 51 points on Sunday afternoon, but they are still in control of the No. 1 overall pick in 2027 NFL Draft.

    It has been revealed that the Titans fell to 1-9 on the season on Sunday afternoon in a rough 51-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium. That marked their fourth straight loss. And, as the Titans hold the key strength of schedule tiebreak, the franchise kept control of the first overall pick in the draft next spring.

    The Titans overtook the Los Angeles Chargers last week for the top spot after the Chargers finally picked up their first win of the season. But on Sunday, after the Chargers fell to the New York Jets 27-24, they joined the Titans at 1-9 on the year. The Miami Dolphins have just a single win to their name, too. The Buffalo Bills rolled over the Dolphins 26-9 on Sunday, marking the team's fourth-straight loss. But the Chargers' loss kept the Dolphins down at the No. 3 overall pick.

    Sources indicate that the Jets now sit at 3-8 on the season. They hold three first-round draft picks in 2027, too, one from the Indianapolis Colts and another from the Cowboys. As things currently stand, the Jets will have both the No. 4 and No. 5 picks.

    Now, Week 11 of the season isn't over yet. The Cincinnati Bengals and Washington Commanders will close things out on Monday night in Maryland. And with three teams at 1-9, the race for the No. 1 pick still has a long way to go.

    For now, the Titans are still in control at the top.

    Sources indicate that as of Sunday, Nov. 22, via Tankathon.

    1. Tennessee Titans (1-9) 2. Los Angeles Chargers (1-9) 3. Miami Dolphins (1-9) 4. Fresh York Jets (3-8) 5. New York Jets (via 3-8 Indianapolis Colts) 6. Arizona Cardinals (3-8) 7. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-7)8. Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) 9. New Orleans Saints (3-7) 10. Atlanta Falcons (3-7)11. Baltimore Orioles (4-7)12. Las Vegas Raiders (4-7)13. Washington Commanders (3-5-1)*14. Houston Texans (4-6)15. New York Jets (via 5-6 Dallas Cowboys)16. New England Patriots (6-4)17. Cleveland Browns (via 6-4 Los Angeles Rams)18. Seattle Seahawks (6-4).

    *The Bengals and Commanders will close Week 11 on Monday night.

    According to recent reports, capitals legend Alex Ovechkin, the NHL's all-time goals king, said Monday that this would be the final season for the 41-year-old. The news didn't come as a surprise, but the timing might have been a little unusual. In any case, the decision adds a lot of significance to Wednesday's home opener against Pittsburgh. That's because you never know whether it might be the last epic Sidney Crosby vs. Ovechkin matchup, as either player could miss future games due to injury or other reasons. Bet $5+ on any of tonight's NHL games to get $150 in bonus bets at DraftKings Sportsbook:.

    Puck drop is set for 7:30 p.m. ET at Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C., and the game will be broadcast on TNT.     Fans can try NHL betting on the best sports betting apps and get bonuses. The SportsLine Projection Model also has picks on games like Penguins-Capitals from its 10,000 simulations, and our experts also offer insights on games every day.

    FanDuel SGP price: +110 (subject to change).

    Recent findings suggest that the Russian said he decided this summer that the 2026-27 campaign would be his last, but that he purposefully waited until ahead of the home opener: "It was vital for me to make this announcement before our first home game, so I have the chance to thank all the people around the game, everyone who has been so important to me and my family and helped me through the good times and tough losses," Ovechkin wrote. "I wouldn't have been able to achieve everything I have in my life without them. I am excited about this season with my teammates, and we will do everything we can to make this year special.".

    Recent findings suggest that in July, Ovechkin signed a one-year deal with the Caps worth $4.25 million – he gets a whopping $4.75 million performance bonus when he plays in his 10th game -- after playing in all 82 last year and putting up yet another 30-goal season with 32. It was his NHL-record 20th 30-goal season. But his average ice time dipped to a career-low 17:27. Through two games this year, Ovechkin is averaging only 13:10 of ice time and has an assist.

    It has been revealed that ovi ranks No. 1 in league history in the regular season in goals (929), power-play goals (331), game-winning goals (141), empty-net goals (72) and overtime goals (27). But if we include playoffs, Ovechkin's 1,006 goals are second behind Wayne Gretzky's 1,016. You know Ovechkin wants that mark too and barring injury should get it. If he scores 20 goals this season, he'll tie Gordie Howe for the most 20-goal campaigns at 22.

    Sources indicate that he's +225 to get one tonight. Ovechkin has scored on 189 different goalies during his NHL career but not yet against Pittsburgh's 25-year-old Arturs Silovs (2-0-1, 2.46 GAA). Silovs was a backup in Vancouver his first three NHL seasons and only got regular time last season with Pittsburgh, so Ovechkin has only faced him twice. Silovs allowed eight goals in two starts last year vs. Washington, splitting them. Ovi did score in one of them, but on an empty net.

    Place your Penguins-Capitals wagers and get up to $1,500 in bonus bets back at BetMGM Sportsbook:.

    Silovs started both of Pittsburgh's first two wins this year, but backup Sergei Murashov was in net for Tuesday's 3-2 home loss to Winnipeg. Crosby was held without a point. He has 1,109 career assists, two shy of tying Ray Bourque (1,111 with Boston) for the most with a single franchise in NHL history. Crosby needs one helper to move past Joe Thornton (1,109) for seventh place on the league's all-time list and is +105 for an assist.

    The NHL is not what it is today without Ovechkin and Crosby, and they entered the league together in 2005. They have faced off 100 times in the NHL, including 25 games in the playoffs. In those 100, they have combined for 231 points. A total of 90 games saw either find the score sheet and 49 had both record a point in the same game.

    Recent findings suggest that they have met in four postseason series, each in the second round. Crosby and the Penguins won the first three series and won the Cup each time. The Capitals won in 2018 and won their first and still only Stanley Cup. They have played 75 regular-season games in the series. Crosby leads 43-28-4 and has 35 goals and 62 assists in those. Ovechkin has 38 goals and 33 helpers.

    In a recent development, the 39-year-old Crosby is in the final year of his contract but has noted he has no plans to retire. He and Ovechkin have joined Howe, Alex Delvecchio, Stan Mikita and Steve Yzerman as the only players in NHL history to play 22 seasons with one franchise.

    In a recent development, "Over the years, obviously, I've developed a friendship with him and have a ton of respect for him," Crosby said to the media Monday with the Ovechkin news. "It's tough, you come into the league at 18 years old, and before we even met, we were built up against each other.".

    It should be Logan Thompson in net for Washington, and he was excellent in his season debut in allowing two goals in a win at defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina last Friday. Last season at home, he was 19-9-5 with a 2.18 GAA and three shutouts. Thompson made two starts vs. Pittsburgh overall last campaign and won both with a 1.50 GAA.

    Sources indicate that the Penguins and Capitals have three meetings left, including Washington's home finale on April 4. That should be quite the Sunday night if both Crosby and Ovechkin are healthy then. Tickets on the secondary market are north of $800 to get in.

    Bet on the NHL and more at FanDuel, where bettors can get up to $250 in bonus bets:.

    We look for any edges in the slog that is the early NHL season, and you'd think the Caps want to send Ovechkin out a winner in his last home opener. And I prefer betting teams in their home openers anyway, simply riding the emotional wave. I hope both Ovi and Crosby score a goal, but that's not something I'd parlay. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

    Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

    The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

    Shesterkin was a major reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

    Recent findings suggest that dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

    Recent findings suggest that new York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

    First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

    Recent findings suggest that upcoming York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

    It has been revealed that the one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a significant commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

    Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

    Industry observers note that however, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

    Industry observers note that markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so promptly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that I've been married for almost 20 years, and you'd think I'd be used to things changing in an instant.
    • In a recent development, I should've remembered that lesson as we headed into Sunday.
    • Before SNF, nobody wanted their QB to face the Vikings.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that I've been married for almost 20 years, and you'd think I'd be used to things changing in an instant. I mean, I've had plenty of practice. Just last Friday, my evening looks switched from nothing (my default choice) to my wife inviting a couple over for board games, to her going to play cards with her sisters. It did turn out to be a quiet night for me. But it reminded me that in our house, a blueprint is, well, more of a suggestion.

    In a recent development, I should've remembered that lesson as we headed into Sunday. From the kickoff to the early games, Week 11 reminded me how quickly things can flip in just a week. Honestly, I came away with more questions than answers. Let's dig into the storylines on some of the things that changed the most.

    Before SNF, nobody wanted their QB to face the Vikings. The only passer to throw for multiple TDs was Jordan Love back in Week 1. Jared Goff in Week 8 was the first to complete over 70% of his passes against Minnesota's defense. And for TEs specifically, Keleki Latu was the sole player at his position to score against DC Brian Flores' unit.

    Brock Purdy and George Kittle raised the bar in Mexico City.

    Of course, the Vikings came in with their usual approach. Purdy saw five or more rushes on 73.3% of his passing attempts. That didn't matter. One, the blitzes only got home once. And two, only one incompletion was the result. Eight of his 10 completed passes turned into a first down or a score. Kittle was the primary fantasy beneficiary of Minnesota opting to treat Purdy like every other QB. But the rest of the receiver corps chipped in, too.

    Target Rate: 26.9% (Evans), 15.4% (Samuel), 15.4% (Allen).

    Air Yard Share: 66.7%, -5.8%, 11.6%.

    First Down per Touch: 100%, 60%, 100%.

    Industry observers note that the "Unc Bowl" was in full effect for HC Kyle Shanahan. None of his aged WRs ran more than 50% of the snaps. But when they were out there, you knew where the ball was going. But the Vikings' secondary couldn't stop them. All four of the 30-plus-year-old pass-catchers were responsible for at least one explosive play. Only Christian McCaffrey got left out in the cold (he still found his way to the end zone). Minnesota's defense looked mortal for the first time all season.

    But the state of the offense is a bigger issue.

    Passing Success Rate: 43.6% (Week 11), 47.1% (Week 10).

    Sources indicate that after a confidence-building week against the Packers with Kirk Cousins fresh off the trade, everything came to a halt against San Francisco. Aaron Jones Sr. and Jordan Mason combined for a 35.3% rushing success rate on early downs, leaving Cousins with 8.6 yards to go in obvious passing situations. Justin Jefferson lost a fumble on a play where he (maybe?) would've scored if he hadn't changed directions. Cousins threw a pick-six. That's two possessions that could've tightened up the score. But as the Vikings were trying to catch up, an old fantasy option returned.

    First Downs Per Route Run: 20.0%.

    Recent findings suggest that T.J. Hockenson came back to a part-time role after missing Week 10 with wrist and chest injuries. However, despite running the fewest routes of any of the starting pass-catchers, only Tai Felton had more targets. Hockenson should be in starting TE slots moving forward. But for Felton, I'd be more wary. The team opted not to place Jordan Addison on injured reserve, expressing optimism that he can be out on the field sooner than the IR designation. So, unless you're in dire need of a receiver, Hockenson should be the only addition from the Vikings off waivers as we head into Week 12.

    Let's review Sunday's expectations for the Bears. The Saints' run defense came into the game allowing the 10th-most yards per game on the ground over their last six contests. Quinshon Judkins was the only starting RB to face Newly introduced Orleans and exit with single-digit PPR points. HC Ben Johnson not only had Kyle Monangai returning from injury, but also the bye to plan.

    Even in the first half, the results were concerning.

    According to recent reports, the Bears' approach to play-calling to start the game was simple: let's establish the run. D'Andre Swift touched the ball on the first four plays. Five of the nine plays on their opening drive were runs. Chicago finished the day with an -8.8% PROE (a season-low mark). Noted another way, the volume was there. But Johnson split the pie up a few ways.

    Swift: 48.0% (Early-Down Touch Rate), 37.0% (Route Share), 53.8%(RZ Snap Rate).

    Swift and Monangai swapped series throughout most of the contest. Luckily for gamers rostering Swift, it was No. 4 who was on the field for Chicago's first TD drive after CJ Donaldson fumbled on their side of the field. Swift got the lone touch from inside the 10-yard line and converted for the score. But therein lies the problem. The combination of a healthy Ben Johnson running game and (theoretically) poor resistance from New Orleans should've garnered more production from anyone carrying the rock. Instead, we got the opposite.

    Rushing Success Rate: 33.3%, Season-low.

    EPA per Rush: -0.36, Season-low.

    Credit to the Saints' defensive line. They met the trio of Bears' rushers at or behind the LoS on 51.9% of their attempts. Monangai wasn't known for being the shiftiest of runners (0.0% forced missed tackle rate), but averaging 1.9 yards after contact didn't help. Swift took all of the short-yardage totes and only came out with one conversion on three attempts. And to make matters worse, Salvon Ahmed mixed in on early downs, siphoning yards away from both.

    I could use the Bears' quick turnaround to face the Lions on Thursday to explain Ahmed's usage. However, season-lows in efficiency, leading to Caleb Williams' third-down environment getting more chaotic (fourth-highest average distance to convert), aren't just about the rotation. And after watching the Lions keep the Bucs' ground game in check, the Bears will need to adjust their run game in order to stay in the race for the top spot in the NFC North.

    I understood Pittsburgh coming out flat against the Bengals in primetime last week. Don't get me wrong, I was surprised in the moment. But I've seen these games between division rivals before. I didn't expect to see the output continue a week later.

    In a recent development, aaron Rodgers' scramble to close out the first quarter was the longest running play for the Steelers on Sunday. If you're rostering Jaylen Warren, apologies in advance. After enjoying the backfield to himself for a stretch, maintaining the starter role and putting up three RB1 finishes, Warren was becoming a staple of fantasy rosters. However, everything's taken a step back.

    Rushing Success Rate: 54.6% (Weeks 1-8), 28.6% (Week 10), 22.2% (Week 11).

    It has been revealed that adj. Yards After Contact per Att.: 4.97, 2.14, 2.67.

    Explosive Play Rate: 12.9%, 7.7%, 0.0%.

    Pittsburgh's biggest play-calling shift was in how often Rodgers dropped back to pass. After having a negative PROE for three straight games, the Steelers were up to +6.3% (fourth-highest on the season). Accordingly, Warren carried the ball just nine times (second-fewest in '26). Philadelphia held him to zero yards before contact on two-thirds of his carries and stuffed him on a third. But that's OK. With more passing, Warren's involvement as a receiver should've kept his fantasy value afloat. However, his QB was also still in a slump.

    Passing Success Rate: 36.7%, 2nd-lowest.

    EPA per Dropback: -0.20, 4th-lowest.

    Pressure-to-Sack Ratio: 62.5%, Season-high.

    The worst part is that the Eagles largely left Rodgers alone. They blitzed him just once. And yet, Rodgers still hit his season-high of five sacks. But I can't blame him. DK Metcalf decided that fighting with the defense was more key than catching the ball. And sure, Germie Bernard earned 10 targets. But again, six of them were on throws of five air yards or less. Rodgers didn't regularly look for him on intermediate or deep throws until the second half.

    The knee-jerk reaction from gamers might be to start Bernard in Week 12. Metcalf might incur a suspension. Rodgers has been more efficient targeting Bernard over Metcalf in multiple games. However, with the Broncos and Texans on their upcoming schedule, I'd keep everybody in black and gold on your bench.

    According to recent reports, my largest concern with Fernando Mendoza starting during this stretch of games for the Raiders was the absence of Brock Bowers. I realize neither he nor HC Klint Kubiak could plan for an injury. But the chasm between Bowers and the rest of the pass-catchers would put anyone in a tough spot. And having to face Denver, coming off its bye, without his de facto WR1 would be a challenge. However, I didn't give enough credence to the idea that Kubiak could prepare his QB to do more with less.

    According to recent reports, to be clear, it wasn't all pretty. The Raiders punted on their first three drives. Mendoza ended the first quarter with just one more completed pass than sacks taken. It wasn't until the half was winding down that Mendoza started to get into the flow. But if there were concerns about whether or not Kubiak was giving Mendoza answers to the defense's questions, the rookie alleviated some of them.

    EPA per Dropback: -0.02 (Week 11), -0.18 (Week 10).

    In-Rhythm Throw Rate: 54.1%, 41.4%.

    It has been revealed that instead of forcing the ball to the middle of the field without his best receiver, Mendoza looked to the perimeter. It was the ideal adjustment given the strengths of the skill players he had on hand. Plus, he's pretty good at it. Mendoza averaged 0.68 EPA per dropback with a 55.6% completion rate on boundary throws. But Mendoza wasn't just aggressive — he was decisive, averaging more throws under 2.6 seconds. Oh, I guess I buried the lede there. All of his TD throws were to the perimeter. And at least one of his target-earners shouldn't be a surprise.

    Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, not much changed for Ashton Jeanty as a runner. Six of his 11 carries came with a defender in the backfield. Denver held him to three or fewer yards on 54.5% of his attempts. But Jeanty came into the game behind only Christian McCaffrey in YPRR and was fifth in YAC per reception. If there was going to be a way to get Mendoza comfortable with the offense, using Jeanty as a receiver was the right call. But there's one more pass-catcher who should be on our radar.

    In a recent development, jack Bech's routes and targets have gone up in three straight weeks. He led the team in looks after Bowers left in Week 10 and was just one shy of Tre Tucker's total in Denver. But with receiving aDOTs of 9.3 and 8.1, Bech won't have the same volatility as a downfield option like Tucker. So even with Bowers likely to return, Bech should be a speculative add if you have the bench space.

    Talk about narratives changing in a week. Jacksonville made multiple additions to the defense before the trade deadline, needed the full four quarters to get by Tennessee but, on paper, looked like one of the favorites to get to the Super Bowl.

    And then the Giants reminded them there are no easy matchups in the NFL.

    To be fair, the signs were there for the Jaguars to face some problems on offense. Starting LT Anton Harrison tore his ACL in Week 5, and C Robert Hainsey missed this game with a knee sprain. Minor injuries to RT Cole Van Lanen and RG Ezra Cleveland only complicated the situation further. Coincidentally, the G-Men were second to the Vikings in blitz rate and ninth in sack rate over their last six games. The outcome was one of Lawrence's worst outings this season.

    Pressure Rate: 42.3%, Season-high.

    Passing Success Rate: 40.0%, 2nd-lowest.

    Completion Percentage Over Expected: -2.1%, 3rd-lowest.

    Sources indicate that jacksonville's matter wasn't just that Lawrence's protection kept breaking down, but how fast things deteriorated. DC Dennard Wilson had his unit getting to Lawrence in 2.5 seconds or faster on 12 of his dropbacks. That's four more than his previous season-high. Accordingly, Lawrence's average time to throw skyrocketed to 3.3 seconds. He started taking more shots downfield (12.1 passing aDOT). Of course, the Giants mounting a multi-score lead by the end of the first half prompted the aggression. But New York reducing them to a one-dimensional offense was the larger issue.

    Rushing Success Rate (on early downs): 27.3%, Season-low.

    Distance to the Sticks (on third downs): 10.8, Season-high.

    Sources indicate that bhayshul Tuten entered the game with foot/ankle injuries, missed time earlier in the game and then left early with a limp. Meanwhile, Chris Rodriguez Jr. ran into a stacked box on every single one of his early-down rushing attempts. Without a running game, Jacksonville turned into a dropback passing unit.

    Sources indicate that let's assume Tuten misses Week 12. Jacksonville has its rematch against the Titans. Rodriguez is healthy. He should be at or near the top of your waiver priority. But I'd be wary about expecting similar target totals for Jakobi Meyers (10) and Josh Cameron (7). Lawrence just attempted more than 45 passes for the first time since Week 7 of last season. Unless you think the Titans can do the same, the offense should go back to its balanced ways in Week 12.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that the annual GM Meetings came and went this week with two significant transactions.
    • Otherwise, the GM Meetings brought a lot of rumors and presumably the groundwork was laid for moves that could be completed later this offseason.
    • In a recent development, the Blue Jays have interest in Diamondbacks second baseman Ketel Marte, who has a full no-trade protection, reports Sportsnet.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the annual GM Meetings came and went this week with two significant transactions. The Braves signed reliever Evan Phillips (three years and $35 million) and the Red Sox signed slugger Jake Bauers (four years and $58 million). Bauers will give Boston some sorely needed home run power. Phillips will pair with Robert Suarez in the late innings for Atlanta.

    Otherwise, the GM Meetings brought a lot of rumors and presumably the groundwork was laid for moves that could be completed later this offseason. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the key offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Saturday's hot stove happenings.

    In a recent development, the Blue Jays have interest in Diamondbacks second baseman Ketel Marte, who has a full no-trade protection, reports Sportsnet. It does not appear a trade is imminent. We ranked Marte among the offseason's top trade candidates despite his odd AWOL incidents the last few seasons. Even at 33, he remains one of the game's best second basemen.

    The Blue Jays went 79-83 this past season largely because of their offense, which ranked dead last in runs and home runs. They also ranked 17th in WAR at second base as All-Star Ernie Clement ran out of steam in the second half. Offensively, Marte is coming off his worst 162-game season since 2018, though he would still represent a clear upgrade for the Blue Jays.

    The Giants continue to decline trade calls about ace righty Logan Webb, reports USA Today. Webb, 30 next week, had his worst full season in the big leagues in 2026, in part due to a nagging knee injury, though he is signed affordably through 2028. San Francisco needs to add to its rotation, not subtract one of the game's best and most durable starters.

    That said, a Webb trade would presumably net the Giants multiple young players and improve the team's talent base. It never hurts to listen, but for now, the Giants seem disinclined to move their best pitcher since Madison Bumgarner was in his prime. Webb and Landen Roupp are the only locks for San Francisco's 2027 rotation at the moment.

    Not surprisingly, the Braves want to add at least one starting pitcher, according to The Athletic. They could also re-sign Raisel Iglesias or bring in another late-inning reliever even after signing Phillips. Chris Sale and Grant Holmes are Atlanta's only returning healthy starters. Bryce Elder (knee), Spencer Schwellenbach (elbow) and Spencer Strider (elbow) all finished the season injured.

    The Braves will give Didier Fuentes, who was so dominant as a reliever this past season, a chance to start in 2027. It will be difficult to count on him for a full season, however. Fuentes, 21, threw a career-high 97 innings between the minors, majors, and postseason in 2026. Atlanta will need to monitor his workload next year. Another starter to soak up innings is a must this offseason.

    In a recent development, the Tigers have interest in free agent left-hander Shota Imanaga, reports MLB.com. Jackson Jobe, Troy Melton, River Ryan, and Framber Valdez are presumably locks for Detroit's rotation. Ty Madden and Keider Montero are depth options. Reese Olson is expected back from shoulder surgery early next year. Still, the Tigers could clearly use another starting pitcher.

    We ranked Imanaga, 33, as the 30th-best free agent available this offseason. He has been very home run prone the last two years (1.9 homers per nine innings), which could make him a good match for what is now called Fifth Third Park. Detroit's stadium tends to play pitcher-friendly, particularly in April and September (and October), when the ball doesn't carry well in the cold.

    The Blue Jays are receiving calls about infielder Ernie Clement and utility man Davis Schneider, reports The Athletic. Teams have also inquired about catcher Brandon Valenzuela, who was a Gold Glove finalist as a rookie in 2026. Toronto reportedly has interest in Jazz Chisholm Jr. as it seeks more of a power bat on the infield, potentially making Clement expendable.

    In a recent development, schneider, 27, had a poor 2026 and spent time in Triple-A, though he is versatile and has hit lefties in spots over the years. There is a shocking shortage of quality right-handed bats throughout baseball right now. Schneider's heavy plate discipline approach and ability to play left field as well as some infield positions make him an interesting enough target this offseason.

    In a recent development, the Cubs, Padres, and White Sox are among several teams pursuing Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, reports the San Diego Union-Tribune. Taira, 26, had a 1.36 ERA in 145 innings for the Seibu Lions in 2026. We ranked him as the 19th-best free agent available this offseason, though he could ultimately wind up in the bullpen given his height (5-foot-8).

    According to recent reports, the Padres and two Chicago teams need starting pitching this offseason (they need multiple starters, really) and would likely use Taira in their rotation, at least to begin the season. For what it's worth, Taira told Sanspo he does not have a preferred destination, geographically. The Cubs, Padres, and White Sox would all give him a chance to pitch for a contender right away.

    Recent findings suggest that the Cardinals have declined trade inquiries into first baseman Alec Burleson and shortstop Masyn Winn, according to the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. St. Louis is also receiving interest in catchers Jimmy Crooks and Pedro Pagés, who are more likely to be traded. Burleson and Winn are off-limits, though, and considered part of the long-term future in St. Louis.

    In a recent development, leo Bernal, who was so impressive during his September call up, and top prospect Rainiel Rodriguez are the future behind the plate for the Cardinals. Pagés is a traditional glove-first backup catcher. Crooks has some offensive upside thanks to his hard-hit ability (exit velocity, etc.), and he rates well as a pitch-framer and thrower. He's an appealing target for catcher-needy teams.

    #130580. What's next for Red Sox after Jake Bauers deal? Plus more intel from the MLB GM Meetings

    📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (874 w)

    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    What's next for Red Sox after Jake Bauers deal? Plus more intel from the MLB GM Meetings

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (874 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that LAS VEGAS — Uncertainty permeated the ARIA Resort & Casino throughout this week's MLB GM Meetings.
    • 1  approaching, media, executives, and all within the baseball industry had some questions: what would baseball look like once the inevitable lockout goes into place?
    • For the Red Sox, a small piece of this peculiar period centers on what to do with former top prospect Kristian Campbell.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that LAS VEGAS — Uncertainty permeated the ARIA Resort & Casino throughout this week's MLB GM Meetings. The looming lockout, of course, played a major role in all of this.

    With Dec. 1  approaching, media, executives, and all within the baseball industry had some questions: what would baseball look like once the inevitable lockout goes into place? What will it look like once it returns? How do you build a roster with such indeterminacy?

    For the Red Sox, a small piece of this peculiar period centers on what to do with former top prospect Kristian Campbell.

    Sources indicate that tuesday (Nov. 17) is a significant date, marking the deadline for teams to decide which players to protect from the Rule 5 draft by adding them to their 40-man roster. Campbell, who did not appear in a massive-league game in 2026, is right now on the 40-man, signing an eight-year $60 million extension just eight games into his 2025 rookie campaign. But after his demotion in late June of that season, Campbell never found his way back to the majors.

    Now, with the lockout upon baseball, according to one source familiar with the situation, Campbell's 40-man spot might be in jeopardy.

    Boston is weighing the possibility of designating Campbell for assignment. When Craig Breslow, the Sox's president of baseball operations, was asked about that Tuesday, he brushed aside the question.

    "I'm not going to speak to that right now," he said "Kristian's part of our organization. We're really happy about that, and we are invested in doing everything we can to get him to perform like he's capable of.".

    Now, if the Red Sox do DFA Campbell, the belief is that he would clear waivers, given his contract and lackluster performance at the minor-league level. Campbell is owed $55 million over the next six seasons, earning $13 million and $16 million over the 2031 and 2032 seasons, respectively. Campbell posted a .256/.383/.380 slash line with eight homers in 462 plate appearances at Triple-A in 2026.

    Because of those figures, one league executive suggested during the GM Meetings that their club would have no interest in Campbell. The exec took it a step further, confidently suggesting that they couldn't envision any team claiming the outfielder, considering the contract.

    Sources indicate that hypothetically, if Campbell is DFA'd, the Red Sox would free up a 40-man roster spot. If he clears waivers, Campbell, who has less than a year of MLB service time, would be outrighted to Triple-A Worcester. The Red Sox could then eventually add him back to the 40-man roster once they feel his production is worthy of another promotion to the parent club.

    None of this would provide the Red Sox with any financial relief unless another team were to claim him. Campbell's contract would still count toward their competitive balance tax payroll even if he were removed from the 40-man roster and remained in the minors.

    Sources indicate that the risk-reward of such a move is something the Red Sox will also have to consider. Campbell has already acknowledged losing confidence following his recent struggles at both the major- and minor-league levels.

    Sources indicate that "He's got a world of potential," said Breslow. "We saw it in the minor leagues when he was coming up. We saw it in the first part of the season in [2025]. Then I think we started to see it in the second half last year, too, [at Worcester]. I still feel like he has a really bright significant-league career ahead of him, and excited to get into spring training and see that manifest on the field.".

    According to recent reports, the Red Sox signed Jake Bauers to a four-year, $58 million deal Friday, giving the club another power bat in their lineup. Willson Contreras will continue to anchor first base while Bauers will serve as the primary DH, filling in for Contreras from time to time.

    Bauers had a breakout season with the Brewers this year, batting .266/.389/.484 with an .874 OPS and 26 homers. The combo of plate discipline and damage in the strike zone intrigued the Red Sox. Furthermore, his ability to lift the ball in the air and use the entire field despite being a lefty gives the Red Sox confidence that he will be productive at Fenway.

    Recent findings suggest that with Bauers part of the fold, though, Jarren Duran's future with the club is even more murky. The Sox are a heavily left-handed offensive club with Bauers, Wilyer Abreu, Masataka Yoshida, Roman Anthony, and Duran in the mix.

    One is likely going to have to go. And Duran, who could earn upwards of $11 million in arbitration next season, appears to be the most likely to be dealt.

    Even before the Bauers signing, multiple sources suggested during the GM Meetings that both the Red Sox and Duran might be better off parting ways via trade.

    Naturally, there is some apprehension.

    Sources indicate that "I've been hearing for three years now about the outfield logjam that we have, but the reality is we haven't had all of our outfielders, including Masataka, healthy at the same time," Breslow remarked. "These things have largely taken care of themselves, unfortunately.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, with the General Manager Meetings now in the rearview mirror, it sure seems like we're playing out the clock in Major League Baseball news until the CBA expires. That would be Dec. 1 at 11:59 p.m. ET. The expectation at this juncture is that the owners will lock the players out and we'll deal with several months of public negotiations. Until then, we can hope to see some player movement, such as the Red Sox signing Jake Bauers.

    In the meantime, let's round up the news and rumors for the day.

    In a recent development, the Padres are in desperate need of starting pitching, should they wish to continue contending. The rotation right now would be Joe Musgrove, Randy Vásquez, JP Sears, Jhony Brito and a shrugging emoji. Sure enough, they are all over the rumor mill for rotation help.

    Industry observers note that the San Diego Union-Tribune reports that they've shown interest in "virtually every starting pitcher" in free agency, "from Tarik Skubal on down. From Matthew Boyd to Shota Imanaga to Dustin May to Kaima Taira." Further, ESPN reports that the Padres have a meeting set up with Skubal but have also shown interest in Freddy Peralta, as well as Michael King, Nick Pivetta and Nick Martinez.

    Expect them to remain active until they land at least two starters.

    In a recent development, it's no secret that the Diamondbacks are open to trading All-Star second baseman Ketel Marte. The Blue Jays have been sniffing around, and now the Orioles have emerged as a suitor, per MLB.com.

    According to recent reports, this one is interesting in that it's not a natural fit. The Orioles have extra infielders and have been said to be shopping infielders in order to land outfield help. Between second and third base, the Orioles have Jackson Holliday, Jordan Westburg, Blaze Alexander, Coby Mayo and Christian Encarnacion-Strand. Presumably, if they are able to swing a deal for Marte, there would be some shuffling with more trades and/or moving someone to the outfield.

    The Mets could have an opening at first base as things currently stand and they've checked in on free agent Ty France, according to the Latest York Post.

    Right now, the Mets are looking at Jared Young (coming off a scary head injury), Mark Vientos and Jorge Polanco as options at first base.

    France, 32 and probably considered a journeyman at this point, had a big season in 2026 for the Padres. He hit .295/.363/.502 (139 OPS+) with 21 homers, 72 RBI and a career-high 4.5 WAR.

    In a recent development, reliever Jonathan Loáisiga is close to signing with a latest team, reports ESPN. The Dodgers are among five teams involved, with the New York Post adding the Phillies, Mets, Yankees and Blue Jays to the mix.

    In 67 outings last season for Arizona, Loáisiga pitched to a 2.42 ERA, 1.03 WHIP and had 48 strikeouts in 67 innings.

    The Yankees have re-signed left-handed reliever Tim Hill to a one-year, $2.25 million deal with a $2.5 million club option for 2028, per ESPN. Hill, 36, made 67 appearances last season with a 4.60 ERA, 1.14 WHIP and 25 strikeouts in 58 ⅔ innings. He held lefties to a .213/.265/.346 line.

    10 most interesting MLB non-tender decisions, including a Red Sox staple and a former Rookie of the Year

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1635 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 20, is an vital date on MLB's offseason calendar.
    • Dozens of players are non-tendered every offseason when teams determine their production no longer warrants the salary.
    • With that in mind, here are the 10 most interesting non-tender decisions ahead of Friday's deadline, using the arbitration salary projections at the indispensable MLB Trade Rumors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    This Friday, Nov. 20, is an vital date on MLB's offseason calendar. It is the deadline for teams to offer 2027 contracts to their arbitration-eligible and pre-arbitration players. The player does not have to sign by Friday's 5 p.m. ET deadline, but he must be offered a contract. If he's not, the player is considered non-tendered and immediately becomes a free agent.

    Dozens of players are non-tendered every offseason when teams determine their production no longer warrants the salary. Adolis García, Nathaniel Lowe, Alek Manoah, and Christopher Morel were among the notable non-tenders last offseason. Go back a few years and big names like Cody Bellinger and Kyle Schwarber were non-tendered.

    With that in mind, here are the 10 most interesting non-tender decisions ahead of Friday's deadline, using the arbitration salary projections at the indispensable MLB Trade Rumors. You can be sure these teams will scour the trade market for these players and try to get something back before making the non-tender official.

    Projected salary: $11.1 million (team control through 2028).

    Duran was a non-tender candidate even before the Jake Bauers signing pushed him out of the everyday lineup. There is no such thing as too many good players, but the Red Sox now have two first basemen (Bauers and Willson Contreras) and four outfielders (Duran, Wilyer Abreu, Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela). Mickey Gasper and Masataka Yoshida are still around too. That's eight players for five lineup spots (first base, DH, three outfield spots). On any given day, three of those guys will be on the bench. Duran, who got MVP votes in 2024, had a 20-20 season in 2026, but it came with a ballooning strikeout rate and a .266 on-base percentage. He has been on the trade block for close to two years now and the writing is on the wall. If the Red Sox are unable to trade Duran this week, there's a real chance he'll get non-tendered Friday given his hefty salary projection.

    Projected salary: $7.7 million (team control through 2028).

    Former No. 1 overall draft picks have been non-tendered in the past (Tim Beckham most recently), just not by the team that drafted them. Non-tendering Torkelson would be a tough look for the Tigers even though he has not developed into the impact hitter he was projected to be coming out of Arizona State. Simply put, the salary is beginning to outweigh the production. Torkelson, 27, is a 25-30 homer bat with one of the league's highest strikeout rates, middling on-base percentages, and no secondary value (defense, baserunning, etc.). That noted, the Tigers do not have an obvious replacement first baseman ready to step in (Colt Keith was the backup in 2026). That, plus the fact that Torkelson has No. 1 pick pedigree, could keep him in Detroit another year.

    Projected salary: $2.3 million (team control through 2029).

    Recent findings suggest that the American League Rookie of the Year in 2024, Gil has battled injuries and ineffectiveness in the two seasons since. The swing-and-miss rate on his fastball went from an elite 28.5% in 2024 to a below-average 18.8% in 2025 and 17.4% in 2026. Gil, 28, spent time in Triple-A this past season and the Yankees moved him into the bullpen late in the year, where the results were so-so. The salary projection is a pittance, particularly for a team with Newly introduced York's payroll, though Gil is now out of minor-league options (he must pass through waivers to go to Triple-A) and doesn't have an obvious role. Because he is a pitcher and breathing, and also has a major award win in the not-too-distant past, the Yankees might be able to find a trade partner this week. If not, Gil is a definite non-tender candidate.

    Projected salary: $7.6 million (team control through 2028).

    In a recent development, A fan favorite and an All-Star this past season, Clement crashed hard in the second half, and the fact of the matter is he has a .295 on-base percentage in his three full seasons with the Blue Jays. Also, the soon-to-be 31-year-old's defensive numbers tumbled this year. Clement's contact skills are elite and he's a versatile, high-energy player. As a utility guy, he's an ace. As an everyday player, he's stretched. Clement's projected salary is hefty for a utility player, particularly one with limited offensive upside who no longer reliably catches the baseball. My guess is the Blue Jays will keep him and live with the salary, but it's not an obvious decision.

    Projected salary: $5.1 million (team control through 2028).

    Similar to Torkelson, non-tendering a former No. 1 overall pick would be a tough look for the Twins, but a clean break might be best for all involved at this point. Lewis, 27, has trended down since his boffo second half in 2023, enough that he was sent to Triple-A for a spell this summer. He's also moved down the defensive spectrum from third base to first base. It's not due to a lack of effort; Lewis is a major tinkerer who has tried all sorts of swing adjustments. It just hasn't come together. A fresh start elsewhere, away from the spotlight of former No. 1 pick and face of the franchise, might be best for him. The budget-conscious Twins could then reallocate the projected $5.1 million elsewhere on the roster. Right now, they can't count on Lewis to hit or have a meaningful impact defensively.

    Projected salary: $3.4 million (team control through 2028).

    In 2023, Gorman slugged 27 home runs and looked like one of baseball's top young power hitters. In the three seasons since, he has not come close to repeating that success. The hope was that moving him to third base, his natural position, would unlock Gorman's offense following the Nolan Arenado trade. That didn't happen, and Gorman spent a major chunk of the summer in Triple-A, where he continued to have a hard time making contact. Now 26, Gorman has a minor-league option remaining and can go to Triple-A again in 2027, but the signs are not subtle. The Cardinals are reportedly seeking a stopgap third baseman until top prospect Jesús Báez is ready, which would likely not be the case if they had any belief in Gorman. That projected $3.4 million salary is a high price for a reclamation project ticketed for the minors.

    Projected salary: $6.9 million (team control through 2028).

    It has been revealed that right-handed power is in short supply throughout baseball and Burger, 31 in April, has hit at least 28 home runs in three of the last four years. He is a one-tool player, though. The home runs come with low batting averages, low on-base percentages, higher-than-average strikeout rates, and little to no defensive or baserunning value. Rangers president of baseball operations Chris Young said his team lacked "grit and toughness," whatever that means, and indicated he wants more hitters who grind out at-bats. That's not Burger, who can hit the ball a mile but is not known for making life tough on pitchers. The $6.9 million projection could be deemed too pricey for a player with such a limited skill set.

    Projected salary: $6.6 million (team control through 2027).

    In a recent development, doval went from the Yankees to the Pirates at the trade deadline, then from the Pirates to the Giants on waivers in September. He's a former All-Star who led the National League in saves in 2023, two things that have boosted his arbitration salaries. Since 2023, Doval has been a middle reliever who was on the outside of the Circle of Trust™ more often than not. The 29-year-old righty still throws very hard. There's nothing wrong with his arm. It's hard to believe he gets hit as hard as he does sometimes. Doval earned $6.1 million in 2026 and a player cannot have a salary cut by more than 20% during his team control years. That would set Doval's minimum 2027 salary at $4.88 million. I wonder if the Giants would offer him a pay cut, say $5.5M or so, and tell him it's either that or a non-tender. That happens a few times a year around the league.

    Projected salary: $6.5 million (team control through 2027).

    A fan favorite in San Diego -- "Ho-ly Sheets!" chants are commonplace during his at-bats at Petco Park -- Sheets has fallen by the wayside a bit with the Padres, so much so that he started just one of their six postseason games this year. The 30-year-old is a platoon player who is good against righties more than great and is a defensive liability at both first base and left field. Realistically, Sheets is a platoon DH, and teams rarely pay well for that role unless they're confident they will get substantial offensive numbers. In the grand scheme of things, the projected $6.5 million isn't much. It is top-of-the-market dollars for this skill set, however.

    Projected salary: $1.4 million (team control through 2029).

    Two years ago, Blanco threw a no-hitter in his eighth career start. This year, he was so far out of the picture that he pitched once in Houston's last 12 games (two innings at the end of a 13-2 blowout), and the Astros opted to start Peter Lambert on two days' rest with a postseason spot on the line in Game 162. Blanco, who is older than you may realize (he turned 33 in August), returned from Tommy John surgery this summer and had a rough go of it. The pitching-needy Astros could send him to Triple-A next season, as he has a minor-league option remaining, but his stuff was diminished after surgery, and again, they didn't trust him late in the year. You would be surprised at how many cheap pitchers get non-tendered every year. Blanco could join them this week.

    #130569. Latest Update: 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame ballot released: 8 things to know, including newcomers, trends and a prediction

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1186 w)
    📖 Baca

    Latest Update: 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame ballot released: 8 things to know, including newcomers, trends and a prediction

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1186 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The ballot for the BBWAA portion of the 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame vote was revealed on Monday, featuring 13 holdovers and 14 newcomers.
    • The full ballot, in alphabetical order, is Bobby Abreu, Jake Arrieta, Jay Bruce, Mark Buehrle, Asdrúbal Cabrera, Starlin Castro, Wade Davis, Brett Gardner, Cole Hamels, Félix Hernández, Torii Hunter, Jon Lester, Andrew Miller, Dustin Pedroia, Andy Pettitte, Buster Posey, Alex Rodriguez, Francisco Rodríguez, Jimmy Rollins, Pablo Sandoval, Ervin Santana, Kyle Seager, Joakim Soria, Chase Utley, Omar Vizquel, David Wright and Ryan Zimmerman.
    • According to recent reports, as a reminder, players must receive votes on at least 75% of the ballots cast to be inducted into the Hall of Fame with the 2027 class.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The ballot for the BBWAA portion of the 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame vote was revealed on Monday, featuring 13 holdovers and 14 newcomers.

    The full ballot, in alphabetical order, is Bobby Abreu, Jake Arrieta, Jay Bruce, Mark Buehrle, Asdrúbal Cabrera, Starlin Castro, Wade Davis, Brett Gardner, Cole Hamels, Félix Hernández, Torii Hunter, Jon Lester, Andrew Miller, Dustin Pedroia, Andy Pettitte, Buster Posey, Alex Rodriguez, Francisco Rodríguez, Jimmy Rollins, Pablo Sandoval, Ervin Santana, Kyle Seager, Joakim Soria, Chase Utley, Omar Vizquel, David Wright and Ryan Zimmerman. Newcomers to the ballot are in bold.

    According to recent reports, as a reminder, players must receive votes on at least 75% of the ballots cast to be inducted into the Hall of Fame with the 2027 class. Those who get at least 5% of the vote can remain on the ballot the following year, and so on, for a maximum of 10 voting cycles. Players who are on the ballot for 10 years without getting 75% of the vote, in addition to players not getting 5% of the vote, fall off the ballot in ensuing years, though that doesn't mean the doors to the Hall are permanently shut.

    In a recent development, the results will be announced on Jan. 19, with the induction set for Cooperstown over the summer.

    Here's everything else you need to know about the Baseball Hall of Fame this offseason.

    Industry observers note that as alluded to earlier, there are two different votes each offseason. The BBWAA vote is for former players who have been retired from Major League Baseball for at least five years. It's the most common method in mainstream Hall of Fame ballot discussions. When you hear stuff like "first-ballot Hall of Famer," it means via the BBWAA vote.

    In a recent development, players who don't make it via the BBWAA vote can get extra chances via committees. That's how, for example, Jeff Kent made it last year. Formerly called the Veterans Committee, the Hall of Fame now uses Era Committees, which are divided into two categories: contemporary baseball (1980 to present) and classic (prior to 1980). The contemporary ballot is then split into two, one for players and one for non-players like umpires, executives, pioneers and managers.

    Sure enough, this time around, it is a non-player Contemporary Baseball Committee, which looks at "managers, umpires and executives whose most significant career impact was realized since 1980.".

    Recent findings suggest that we'll dive further into this group as we get closer to the Dec. 6 vote.

    In a recent development, giants legend Buster Posey joins the ballot, and he's one of those cases where I don't think a bunch of people need to delve deeply into his numbers. More than statistics, sometimes we get "feel" guys, as in, you just know he's a Hall of Famer. Posey qualifies there, I would think, for 75% of the electorate. We'll obviously do a deeper dive in the coming weeks, but even without the longevity component (Posey only played in parts of 12 MLB seasons), I think he's in.

    Sources indicate that as for the rest of the first-timers, the best case would be Jon Lester. Given the way a lot of similar starting pitchers have been treated in voting in recent years, my hunch is he'll be able to hang around on the ballot, but he has a major uphill battle in order to get in.

    Then you're looking at Brett Gardner, Ryan Zimmerman, Kyle Seager, the short peak of Jake Arrieta and relief work of Andrew Miller. Good players worth mentioning, of course, but they won't sniff the Hall and it seems likely all behind Posey and Lester are one-and-dones on this ballot, as they'll fall short of 5% of the vote.

    Industry observers note that this is the sixth year for Alex Rodriguez on the ballot, which means it's the sixth time that I point out that we don't really need much time to go over his case. His numbers say he's one of the 10 best position players of all time, but his ties to PEDs are keeping him out to this point.

    Recent findings suggest that he did rise from 37.1% of the vote in 2025 to 40% last time, a upcoming high-water mark. The progress is too modest to believe it's trending toward him getting in, but the number this year is certainly worth watching. If he somehow makes a leap to the 50% range, a deeper conversation might be in order.

    While some voters don't mind sending in blank ballots to prove some sort of nebulous point, most impose limits on themselves. Whether it's the actual rule of 10 or some voters saying they'll only vote, for example, for a maximum of three players on any given ballot, relatively weak ballots can leave openings for the best players to show huge gains. With Carlos Beltràn and Andruw Jones getting in last year and only one strong first-year candidate, perhaps Chase Utley can benefit.

    Utley is only in his fourth year on the ballot, but he's already made significant gains:.

    It has been revealed that he only needs to add 15.9 points after jumping nearly 20 last voting cycle. The situation is ripe for Utley to either get all the way in or get close enough to where he probably makes the Hall of Fame in 2028.

    Some of us are pushing to lower the Hall of Fame standard on modern starting pitchers, given the decreases in workload and how it affects their career numbers. We might be making some headway, but it's still tough sledding. Here are the holdover starting pitchers and their standing:.

    Industry observers note that the bar for relievers to make the Hall of Fame is justly pretty high. We recently saw Billy Wagner make a late move and make it in his last try on the BBWAA ballot. Francisco Rodríguez has had four chances on the ballot and gotten between 7.8% and 11.8% of the vote thus far.

    K-Rod ranks sixth all time in saves and has good rate stats. He's worth tracking as it relates to three active relievers. Kenley Jansen is third in saves with a similar number of innings pitched to K-Rod. Craig Kimbrel is fifth and has more than 100 fewer innings pitched. Aroldis Chapman is ninth and in the ballpark of Kimbrel in workload to this point.

    In a recent development, if K-Rod continues to have trouble making headway toward induction, does that mean Kimbrel and Chapman will have trouble as well? What about Jansen?

    Sources indicate that who else is back on the ballot? A quick look:.

    Posey is a lock. If the committee era chooses Bochy, Baker and/or Sabean, that would be some nice San Francisco flavor, too, right? I'll predict that committee ballot at a later date, though.

    I'll also say Utley's good roll here continues with a relatively weak ballot (at least when you factor in what the PED stain has done to some guys).

    On the player side, my 2027 Hall of Fame class prediction is Buster Posey and Chase Utley.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.
    • That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

    That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

    As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

    When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

    Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

    Industry observers note that loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

    It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

    Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

    Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

    Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

    Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

    Industry observers note that this season's NBA Rookie of the Year race has the potential to be one of the closest in league history. While there is no 65-game requirement to win the award — unlike MVP, Defensive Player of the Year and All-NBA honors — playing as many games as possible will be paramount this season in order to claim Rookie of the Year.

    Sources indicate that that's why Chicago Bulls forward Caleb Wilson faces an uphill climb to win the honor after fracturing his right hand earlier this month. Wilson is set to miss the next 3-5 weeks and will likely lose serious ground to others in his class. He currently has the sixth-best odds (+4000) on FanDuel Sportsbook to win Rookie of the Year.

    It has been revealed that during the first month of the season, three players have separated themselves at the top: Yaxel Lendeborg, Cameron Boozer, and Darius Acuff Jr. While it's not a guarantee one of those players wins it, if the season ended today, those would be the top vote-getters.

    Darryn Peterson and AJ Dybantsa — the first two picks of the 2026 NBA Draft — have some ground to make up during the next four months to get back in the mix.

    With the regular season almost a quarter of the way complete, let's dive into our first Rookie of the Year rankings. All odds via FanDuel.

    With Steph Curry out, Lendeborg has continued to step up. The oldest player drafted in the first round is coming off a lackluster showing against the Spurs in the NBA Cup, but before that he had three straight games of 23+ points. He is shooting 48.6% from the field and 41.4% from 3. Lendeborg didn't start shooting 3s on a consistent basis until he got to Michigan last season, so knocking down that percentage on 5.4 attempts per night is a positive sign. Fourteen games into the season, Lendeborg is the favorite.

    In a recent development, boozer's raw stats aren't as good as Lendeborg's or even Acuff's, but his impact goes well beyond the box score. His feel for the game is elite for a 19-year-old. Boozer keeps getting better and better as a processor as he continues to log more minutes. The Grizzlies have been one of the league's surprising teams this season. Boozer deserves a ton of credit for that. He wins everywhere he goes, whether at the high school, college, or professional level.

    Sources indicate that acuff just turned 20 last week. In 13 games as a teenager, he averaged 25.5 points per game and became the first teenager in NBA history to score at least 275 points and dish out 80 assists in his first 11 games. Acuff is a special offensive talent who is being asked to do more than any rookie in his class. Sacramento is a very bad basketball team, but Acuff makes the Kings somewhat fun to watch. That's a huge credit to him.

    The Jazz have been decimated by injuries this season and are presently riding a 12-game losing streak. The one bright side amidst some very bad basketball is how good Peterson has been during that stretch. Peterson had a five-game stretch in which he scored 20 points in each game and shot the ball well from 3. Peterson is the future of Utah's franchise, so getting him as many reps as possible on and off the ball should be the priority.

    It has been revealed that dybantsa, the No. 1 overall pick, is averaging 14 shot attempts per game during his first 10 appearances as a pro. He should be taking even more shots. The way the Wizards are using him is confusing at times. Dybantsa is in somewhat of a weird situation because of the Wizards' roster. Washington handed Trae Young a huge contract this offseason that is already aging poorly. Dybantsa should be the focus of the offense. He should be touching the ball and shooting it even more than he is already. I have been impressed with Dybantsa's defense this season.

    Sources indicate that hello and welcome to the last full work week before Thanksgiving. In Major League Baseball, that usually means a slow news week. Those of us wanting a flurry of moves before the CBA expires on Dec. 1 are starting to lose a little hope, but hey, it's still possible. We can start with a fresh batch of rumors and wait for something to come to fruition.

    As for the news and rumors for Monday, Nov. 16, let's go.

    The Orioles are "operating with the intent of adding" a left-handed starting pitcher, according to the Baltimore Banner. They have extended a qualifying offer to Trevor Rogers and though he's expected to decline it, a reunion remains possible. If not, the Orioles are also reportedly interested in lefty free agents Kris Bubic, Matthew Boyd and David Peterson.

    In a recent development, rogers is the best option here. He finished last season with a 2.90 ERA in his last 20 starts. CBS Sports ranked him as the No. 3 free agent this offseason and the best non-Tarik Skubal pitcher on the market. Here's part of the write-up:.

    Industry observers note that rogers was never able to fully work off the early season stinkers that inflated his ERA, though this is free agency, and ERA is close to the last thing on the minds of interested teams. You're looking forward in free agency, not backward. The underlying performance indicators are very strong, specifically the ability to get chase and avoid the barrel with four pitches (four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper) that light up analytical models. Rogers also has a fifth-pitch cutter and has shown the ability to hammer the strike zone the last two years.

    It has been revealed that as things stand, the Orioles' rotation starts with right-handers Kyle Bradish and Shane Baz. Cade Povich is a left-handed option, but they'd clearly like someone else who could qualify as a frontline starter from the left-handed side.

    Former Cy Young winner Sandy Alcantara has been involved in trade rumors for years and the Marlins never end up moving him. More of the same this offseason? Probably.

    "I expect Sandy to be on the Marlins next year," general manager Peter Bendix told MLB Network.

    Sources indicate that alcantara, 31, was 13-11 with a 3.87 ERA, 1.23 WHIP and 153 strikeouts in an MLB-best 214 innings last season. He also grabbed three saves down the stretch as the Marlins started experimenting with using starters in relief on their bullpen day between starts. The 2022 Cy Young winner missed all of 2024 after having Tommy John surgery and started to show flashes of his old self last season. He's now making $21 million in 2027 before hitting free agency.

    If the Marlins contend, he'll surely stay put, but if they fall out of contention, it'll be another round of trade rumors.

    In a recent development, free agent left-hander A.J. Minter is getting a lot of interest, per MLB Network. Coming off a season in which he was productive for both the Mets and Twins (in all, a 2.56 ERA, 1.05 WHIP and 41 strikeouts in 45 ⅔ innings), he's being chased by at least the Blue Jays, Nationals, Phillies, Rangers and Royals.

    Industry observers note that though he's closed on occasion, Minter has been a quality setup man for most of his 10 MLB years, especially with the Braves in the 2020-24 range. He has good playoff numbers, too, with a 2.88 ERA in 20 career postseason appearances.

    The Brewers have acquired right-handed reliever Ryan Walker from the Giants for two minor-league pitchers, the team announced late Sunday. Walker, 30, was up and down in his four years with the Giants, which included time as a closer. He had a 1.91 ERA, 10 saves and 2.8 WAR in 2024, but lost the job of closer during a sub-par 2025 season. Last year, he pitched to a 7.16 ERA and 1.81 WHIP in 32 ⅔ innings.

    We have plenty of examples of the Brewers buying low on a player and ending up getting the best version of him, so Walker is the latest to keep an eye on here.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Philadelphia 76ers are off to a fantastic start to the 2026-27 season at 12-3, good for first in the Eastern Conference, and perhaps most encouraging for the Sixers is that they're winning without looking like a team playing at its absolute peak.

    After a huge offseason adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, the Sixers still look like a team figuring out how best to work together, but when it comes time in the fourth quarter to find a way to win, they manage to get the job done. Tyrese Maxey is leading the way with Brown quickly finding his rhythm, but James and Joel Embiid in particular still seem to be feeling it out early in the season.

    According to recent reports, james, who has never averaged less than 20.9 points per game in his previous 23 seasons, is averaging just 15.1 points per game and his 44.3/22.5/71.7 shooting splits are all career lows or close to it. As James figures things out, ESPN reported that a Sixers source claimed James "asked coaches to be patient with him as he expects to find his rhythm and get his conditioning in line by December as he ramps up.".

    That report hit social media and caught James' attention, with the 41-year-old star denying ever saying that.

    ESPN didn't report a direct quote from James, and it's very possible the Sixers source offered an anecdote that paraphrased James and used the word patience when James never did. That then ended up on a social media graphic and prompted James to shoot it down.

    It has been revealed that what's fascinating here is it's not a scathing report or even anything particularly juicy. James is struggling with his shot early in the year and seems to be figuring out exactly where he fits in the offense alongside Maxey, Brown and Embiid as a scorer. He's still doing plenty of things well -- including leading the team with 6.9 assists per game and just took over third all-time in assists in NBA history -- and the Sixers are still winning even with James ice cold with his jumper, which history suggests will turn around at some point.

    Patience would be prudent from the Sixers with James, whether he wants to use that word or not, and it seems like a matter of when, not if, he gets shots to start falling and the Philly offense becomes even more dynamic.

Skubal brings four swing-and-miss pitches to the table (four-seamer, changeup, slider, curveball), a near MLB-best ability to limit exit velocity, and elite strike-throwing ability (MLB's third-lowest walk rate since 2023). Build an ace starter in a lab and he would look a lot like Skubal. He'll play the entire 2027 season at age 30, and given the things teams can do with pitchers these days, Skubal figures to remain a frontline starter for most of a long-term contract. He's the only true balance-of-power player available in free agency this offseason. Skubal can swing a division race and a postseason series all by himself.".

    Recent findings suggest that will he set the record for the biggest contract ever signed by a pitcher? Will Skubal fetch the highest average annual salary for a pitcher? Will he top $400 million? Those are all reasonable questions to ask. First, though, there's a question to be asked about the teams that are already pursuing him the most vigorously. That question is, which team needs him the most? We're restricting our discussion to the five teams that have been most reliably linked to Skubal so far this offseason. We're already hearing reports of surprise teams, and it's always possible a surprise late bidder will enter the fray and even win his signature, but for now, these five clubs are the favorites. This, then, is an ordering of those teams based on which desperately needs a talent like Skubal in order to reach their goals in 2027 and beyond. Let's get to it, in order from "needs him the most" to "needs him but not as urgently as the teams ahead of them" ….

    It has been revealed that the Cubs are in contention mode and in need of roster improvements if they're going to run down the world champion Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Central. The rotation is without question the most pressing need for Chicago. Shota Imanaga, Matthew Boyd, David Peterson, and deadline acquisition Clay Holmes are all free agents. Justin Steele hasn't taken the mound at the significant-league level since early in the 2025 season thanks to UCL surgery and a halting recovery process. While he's expected to be ready for 2027, he's not exactly a known quantity right now. Young upsider Cade Horton may not be back until midseason after undergoing Tommy John surgery, and Ben Brown, who recently had neck surgery, may be on a similar timeline. So, yes, the Cubs need a lot of rotation help, and Skubal would give them the true frontline ace they'd lack even if everyone were healthy. Unfortunately for the Cubs fans, it sounds like the Ricketts aren't willing to be truly competitive for his services.

    Coming off the grave disappointments of 2026, the Mets could certainly use a headline-grabbing addition to improve their chances in 2027 and inspire a surely disaffected fan base. Beyond that, the Mets need more starting pitching to accompany promising young Nolan McLean. Christian Scott seems like a lock, but he doesn't project as a frontliner. They have some depth options for the back end, but they need a true needle-mover like Skubal at the very front. That's especially the case in what figures to be a hotly competitive NL East in 2027. Thus far, David Stearns and owner Steve Cohen sound committed to making a good-faith run at Skubal.

    The Padres have a lot of work to do if they're going to earn a fourth straight playoff appearance. Speaking of which, the rotation is crying out for help right about now. They lost Dylan Cease to free agency last winter, and this time Michael King may be bound elsewhere, too. The Pads declined their club option on Nick Pivetta, and while they hope to bring him back on more favorable terms, there's no guarantee they'll be able to do that. Yes, Joe Musgrove will be back, but how much can he give them and how effective will he be? They'll need even more help if Adrian Morejon, a lockdown bulk reliever and possible starter-conversion project, signs elsewhere. Skubal's made to order, and signing the top talent on the market would be a strong signal by new owners José E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones that the team's recent tradition of spending and contending won't be fading away.

    According to recent reports, the Dodgers self-evidently needed Skubal enough to acquire him from the Detroit Tigers leading up to the deadline and do so at significant cost. On paper, the Dodgers aren't as desperate for rotation help as the teams ahead of them on this list, but there's still a need. Yoshinobu Yamamoto is a certifiable ace, but behind him Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow are established health and durability risks. Shohei Ohtani is something of an unknown, at least insofar as his pitching is concerned right now, and thus far Roki Sasaki and Emmet Sheehan have not proved worthy of being relied upon. One can squint and see the Dodgers' current championship window closing in the reasonably near future, which means that's all the more reason to push the chips in now. Retaining the elite services of Skubal would greatly aid the cause in 2027.

    Eyeball a rotation that already includes Dylan Cease, José Soriano, and Trey Yesavage, and you might think it doesn't need much more. And maybe it doesn't. As a matter of principle, though, any team with contending aspirations should be interested in a top-shelf ace when he hits the market. The Jays, who in recent years have invested in the roster at commendable levels, are no doubt dreaming of a Skubal-Cease one-two punch that would be the envy of, oh, every other team in baseball. There's also depth to think about. In particular, Cody Ponce is a bit of an unknown coming off knee surgery that ended his 2026 season in the middle of his first start. Addressing the offense probably should be more of a priority for the Jays this winter, but, again, it's Tarik Skubal, and the likes of Tarik Skubal make any team better.
